title: Total Fencing Cost of an Isosceles Right Triangular Pen as a Function of Hypotenuse
originalTopic: Theory and Examples: Applied Function Modeling
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A pen in the shape of an isosceles right triangle with legs of length x ft and hypotenuse of length h ft is to be built. If fencing costs $5/ft for the two legs and $10/ft for the hypotenuse, write the total construction cost C as a function of h.

steps.title: Express Total Cost in Terms of x and h
steps.explanation: The triangle has two legs of length x ft costing $5/ft each (totaling 5(2x) = 10x dollars) and one hypotenuse of length h ft costing $10/ft (totaling 10h dollars).
steps.why: Total fencing cost is the sum of the lengths of each boundary segment weighted by its unit cost per foot.

steps.title: Relate Leg Length x to Hypotenuse Length h
steps.explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem for an isosceles right triangle, 2x^2 = h^2, so x = (sqrt(2)/2)h.
steps.why: The legs of an isosceles right triangle are equal in length and meet at a 90-degree angle.

steps.title: Substitute x into the Cost Equation and Factor
steps.explanation: Replace x with (sqrt(2)/2)h in C = 10x + 10h and factor out 5h to obtain C(h) = 5(2 + sqrt(2))h dollars.
steps.why: Eliminating x expresses the total construction cost as a direct linear function of h alone.
